subject: ConcordAI — post-call cost alignment and batching pilot checklist
content:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Morales <evan@concord.ai>, Priya Singh <priya.s@concord.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: ConcordAI — post-call cost alignment and batching pilot checklist

Hi Evan / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we have alignment on scope and economics before we put together the formal pilot SOW. I tried to keep this tight so your procurement and engineering teams can scan quickly.

Key pain & goals (what you said)
- Cost sensitivity: you have a hard monthly inference budget of ~$75k for the first 3 months of the pilot (production-ish traffic).
- Latency: 95th percentile target ~220ms for the user-facing inference path; batch-tolerant background features can be higher.
- Quality: must match current fine-tuned model behavior for slot filling and intent normalization (we agreed to include a focused eval set).
- Data controls: VPC/private deployment for the pilot is preferred but initial testing can run in hosted with strict logging and retention rules.

Token economics and levers we discussed
- Baseline tokens per request: your traffic estimates suggested ~420 input tokens and ~120 avg output tokens for a typical assistant prompt.
- Recommended model family: quantized Llama-3 16k variant for latency/cost balance (we suggested q4/8 profile).
- Batching: batching 6–10 concurrent requests for the user path vs 20–40 for async jobs; expected per-token unit cost drop of ~28–40% depending on concurrency.
- KV/Prefix caching: for repeated prompts (FAQ/common user personas) we can expect another 8–12% token reduction via prefix caching.
- Fallback routing: mixing a cheaper 8k model for short prompts when quality is equivalent — small upside but useful under peak load.

Preliminary TCO snapshot (illustrative)
- Estimated token run-rate at 250k end-user requests/day (peak traffic window): ~13M tokens/day -> ~390M tokens/month.
- With suggested batching/caching/quantization: projected cost range = $45k–$70k/mo (hosted, usage-based) depending on achieved batch hit-rate and quantization tradeoffs.
- If you require Dedicated capacity / Reserved pool, we can map that to a commit that smooths unit costs further; we have examples in the attached spreadsheet.

Proposed pilot scope (minimal viable to prove economics & ops)
1) 4-week integration + baseline measurement: integrate SDK, run real traffic to collect token distribution and latency profiles. (Owner: Concord eng + Redwood SE)
2) 6-week performance tuning: enable batching and prefix caching, deploy q4 quantized variant in staging, collect quality/regression metrics on the eval set. (Owner: Redwood infra + Concord eng)
3) 4-week low-volume ramp: run a controlled production slice at 5–10% traffic to validate SLA and run-rate. (Owner: Concord product + CS)

Deliverables we will provide
- A populated concord_tco_modeling_v1.xlsx with per-token unit cost sensitivity and commit vs usage comparisons.
- Pilot one-pager and success criteria (attached).
- A short evaluation harness (shared Drive link) for your QA team to validate outputs.

Immediate asks / next steps (actionable)
- Evan / Priya: confirm the $75k/mo hard constraint and whether the pilot can accept a range +/-10% during measurement (Y/N).
- Evan: please introduce your procurement contact (Daniel?) — we need a light MSA/POC path for pilot start.
- Concord eng: share a small sample of anonymized request traces (1–2 days) so we can pre-run token distribution modeling.
- Redwood: we will return a filled TCO spreadsheet and a pilot SOW draft by Aug 20.

Thanks — if anything above is off, call it out and I’ll update.

Best,
Irene Choi
Manager, Solutions — Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0191

Attachments: concord_tco_modeling_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), pilot-scope-onepager.pdf (one-pager)

Irene —

Appreciate the crisp recap — looks accurate from our side. A couple clarifications:
- The $75k/month is the absolute cap for this pilot bucket (we can float a little during measurement but procurement needs a firm upper bound).
- Daniel Owens is our procurement lead (daniel.owens@concord.ai) — loop him in for contract language and PO cadence.
- We can share one anonymized day of traces this week; will normalize PII on our side.

We’re keen to see the TCO spreadsheet and the SOW by Friday (Aug 20). If we can validate the numbers quickly we should be able to start integration in the first week of Sept.

Thanks,
Evan
Head of Product — ConcordAI

Thanks for the recap — two short technical notes from my side that affect the TCO run: 
1) For the latency target (95th @ 220ms) we'll aim for a batching window tuned to 30–40ms scheduling plus the model runtime; if you can't accept that extra queuing on the user path we should scope a hybrid: small per-request hot-path with higher unit cost + larger async batches for non-critical tasks.
2) The q4 quantization profile gives good cost wins but adds a small delta in hallucination-sensitive outputs; we’ll lock an eval harness to measure exact delta and include an automatic fallback to a higher-precision variant for flagged failures.

Irene, I can own the runtime tuning and measurement deliverable. Evan — once you drop the sample traces I’ll pre-run the token distribution model and return per-scenario batch hit-rate assumptions.

Ben
Senior Systems Engineer — Redwood Inference
